headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because oh-my-openagent can handle provider auth and broad egress while PaddleOCR processes documents/images via API calls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: oh-my-openagent can ingest AGENTS.md, README.md, session history, and runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images that could contain attacker-controlled text. A plausible bridge exists if A forwards OCR output into its instruction context, but that interaction is not directly documented here, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_a forwards OCR text into prompts or MCP messages without sanitization
IF agent_b output is copied into agent_a's instruction context or AGENTS.md-driven workflow
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OCR output into prompts
Add a fixed delimiter and provenance tag around B output
Review any MCP hook that reads document text
Use a manual copy step for untrusted OCR results
requires-engineering: add content provenance tracking between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches provider authentication data, session history, project code, and AGENTS.md, and has broad network egress; agent_b processes documents and images via API calls. If A sends B-processed content or auth-bearing context to external services, sensitive material can leave the workspace by default. The pairwise path is plausible from the profiles, so this is high.
conditions: IF agent_a includes provider auth prompts or session history in outbound requests
IF agent_b receives documents containing secrets or personal data and returns them to agent_a for further transmission
mitigations: Remove secrets from inputs before OCR
Restrict agent_a egress to approved endpoints only
Use redaction before any handoff from B to A
Audit outbound payloads for auth data
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances and writes to installation/config paths, while agent_b has allowlisted network egress and API-based processing. They do not obviously share a writable directory, but both can act on the same project artifacts and external resources, creating a realistic coordination conflict if run concurrently. The overlap is plausible but not proven, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project files or generated artifacts
IF agent_a launches multiple instances against the same installation while agent_b is processing the same documents
mitigations: Serialize access to shared project files
Run each agent in a separate workspace
Lock generated artifacts during OCR and post-processing
Check for concurrent writes before saving
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: oh-my-openagent can create team messages/tasks and use LSP/MCP actions, while PaddleOCR turns documents into extracted text that A may treat as authoritative. If B's OCR output is passed to A without verification, A can propagate extraction errors into downstream actions. The pathway is plausible from the profiles, but not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_a uses OCR text as source-of-truth for tasks or messages
IF extracted text from agent_b is not checked against the original document before action
mitigations: Require human review before sending tasks or messages
Compare OCR output against source snippets
Mark OCR text as untrusted in downstream prompts
Limit A to drafting only, not executing actions
requires-engineering: add verification against source documents

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles provider authentication data and session history, while agent_b handles documents and images. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a generic compliance gap is visible: if regulated data is placed into B and then routed through A's broader egress, policy violations could occur. This is lower confidence and lower blast radius than the other risks.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed by agent_b
IF agent_a transmits those results to services outside the required residency or retention boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document the allowed data classes for each agent
Turn off unnecessary logging where possible
Review retention settings before processing
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
